text:
Alice Chen: Quick follow-up to the FlashAttention RFC — after running the early integration tests, I have a few open questions about v2 vs v3 perf deltas and how we should wire kernel selection into the runtime. TL;DR: seeing mixed wins depending on seq len and GPU, want to confirm strategy.

Miguel Torres: Great — can you paste the microbench numbers? :eyes:

Alice Chen: Sure, ran microbench with our standard GPT-like config (12B, fp16, causal, single head-shard):
```
A100 80GB: seq=512 -> baseline (custom FEL) 1.0x, FA-v2 1.6x, FA-v3 1.7x
A100 80GB: seq=2048 -> baseline 1.0x, FA-v2 2.0x, FA-v3 2.3x
H100 80GB: seq=512 -> baseline 1.0x, FA-v2 1.9x, FA-v3 2.2x
H100 80GB: seq=4096 -> baseline 1.0x, FA-v2 2.7x, FA-v3 3.1x
Notes: small sequences (<=128) sometimes slower on FA-v3 due to kernel launch/tiling overhead. Memory peak dropped ~10-18% on v3 for long seqs.
```

Priya Nair: Interesting. Did you test with packed batching (variable-length packing) vs fixed padding? FlashAttention's perf is sensitive to how padded tokens are handled.

Alice Chen: Yes — with packing (we avoid padding across sequence dim) the wins are better for v3 at mid seq lengths because it reduces wasted work. But our continuous-batching path currently pads to max in batch, so we see smaller gains there.

Dan Kline: Two integration points to consider: kernel API (inputs/outputs shape contract) and KV-cache interaction. FA-v3's API expects packed/contiguous q/k/v and offers a packed-only fast path — we need a plan for our KV cache layout. Right now our KV cache is per-request tiled chunks with alignment for cuBLAS.

Miguel Torres: Agreed. Also note thread-safety and workspace allocation: FA-v3 relies on dynamic shared memory and a temp workspace per CUDA stream. On multi-tenant Dedicated nodes we observed more fragmentation with existing allocator. We should use a per-device scratch allocator and pre-claim worst-case workspace for long-seq launches.

Alice Chen: Implementation proposal: 1) runtime exposes a kernel registry with entries: kernel_id, min_seq, max_seq, gpu_whitelist (compute capability), packing_hint (packed|pad), mem_overhead_estimate. 2) selector uses model metadata + request seq distribution telemetry to pick kernel per-inference (or per-route). 3) fallback to baseline kernel for unsupported combos. Example config snippet: 
```json
{
  "kernel_id": "flashattn_v3_fp16",
  "min_seq": 128,
  "max_seq": 8192,
  "gpu_whitelist": ["sm_90", "sm_80"],
  "packing_hint": "packed",
  "mem_overhead_mb": 512
}
```

Priya Nair: That looks reasonable. A couple of tradeoffs: 
- If we force packed layout to hit v3, we might increase serialization latency because packing requires pre-processing.
- For small-latency requests (seq<128, single-token streams) the baseline kernel + prefix cache is better.

Dan Kline: For runtime rollout we should do canary by route with AB split and measuring p50/p95/p99 and cost delta. Also surface telemetry: kernel_used, seq_length, workspace_bytes, gpu_model, fallback_reason. Those are essential for automatic fallback and autoscaling heuristics.

Miguel Torres: From microbench to e2e, expect smaller effective gains because network + prefix-copy + decoding loop overhead dominate at token-at-a-time generation. For our streaming mode where we generate 1-4 tokens per request the win is ~1.1-1.4x. For batched completion workloads the win approaches the microbench numbers.

Alice Chen: Good call. I also saw a weird regression on an older V100 dev node where FA-v3 falls back to a slower kernel because it lacks a required SM feature; we should blacklist older GPUs at runtime and avoid attempting v3 there.

Priya Nair: What about mixed precision and quantization? FA-v3 has kernels for fp16 and bfloat16. We still need to route int8 quantized models to a different path (Cutlass/Quant kernels) — mixing them will complicate selector logic.

Miguel Torres: Suggestion: separate kernel dimensions in registry: dtype dimension (fp16, bf16, int8), and have the selector treat dtype as a hard constraint. For int8 we route to our quant inference kernels (existing path). That keeps FlashAttention only for fp/bf16 workloads.

Dan Kline: Action items: 
- Miguel: run full e2e AB on a subset of production routes (short streaming, medium batch, long context) and capture kernel telemetry.
- Priya: validate correctness for masked attention edge-cases (left-padding, causal masks, edge-case EOS tokens) with v3 fused kernels.
- Alice: add kernel registry prototyping in runtime repo, include simple scoring function + canary config.

Miguel Torres: I'll start the AB runs tonight. Quick note on metrics: please track p50/p95/p99 decode latency per-token and tokens/sec per-GPU as primary. Also track tail OOM/fallback counts.

Alice Chen: Thanks — also adding a follow-up: we might want an autotuner job that gathers perf curves (seq vs throughput) per GPU per kernel and uploads to config service, so selector can pick empirically.

Priya Nair: +1 for autotuner. Saves ops from hardcoding thresholds.

infra-bot: Canary deploy started for route "/gen-large-context" on cluster "dedicated-gpu-3" by Miguel Torres — 20% traffic split.

Dan Kline: One more implementation caution: license and shipping. FlashAttention v3 includes third-party kernel code under its license — legal has flagged redistributability for our Private customers. Need to confirm allowed distribution in on-prem packages.

Alice Chen: Good catch — I'll loop in legal and product. For now assume hosted & dedicated can use it; private may require opt-in or alternate fallback.

Miguel Torres: Initial AB results (first 2 hours): route /gen-long-context (batch) saw end-to-end tokens/sec +95% and p99 token latency down 37%. Streaming route /chat-low-latency saw tokens/sec +18% and p99 down 12%. Fallback rate 0.6% due to older nodes.

Priya Nair: Any correctness diffs in model outputs? We need to run eval prompt sets for regressions.

Miguel Torres: Ran eval on our regression suite (prompt sets ~1k examples) — no functional regressions observed beyond numeric rounding differences. We'll run a larger overnight pass.

Alice Chen: Ok let's proceed with the plan: prototype registry + selector, telemetry additions, autotuner in parallel, AB runs for 48h, legal check for redistribution. If no regressions and stable telemetry, roll to 100% for Dedicated and Hosted.

Dan Kline: Sounds good. I'll open RFC follow-up PR for kernel registry interface and a runtime ticket for telemetry fields.

Alice Chen: Thanks all. :thumbsup:

Miguel Torres: :rocket:

Priya Nair: :eyes:

infra-bot: Canary deploy updated: /gen-large-context -> 35% traffic after successful health checks.
